description: Probability theory and statistics built for computer scientists, with every distribution simulated in R before and after it is derived. Taught to the depth of a full probability course for computer scientists.
modelledOn: Ross, A First Course in Probability
Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Probability
Walpole, Myers, Myers and Ye, Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists
outcomes: Compute probabilities of events with counting, conditional probability, independence and Bayes' theorem.
Work with discrete and continuous random variables, their PMFs, PDFs, CDFs, expectations and variances.
Recognise and apply the standard distributions, including Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, Poisson, uniform, exponential and normal.
Use moments and moment generating functions to derive properties and sums of random variables.
Apply the law of large numbers and central limit theorem and construct confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.
Simulate random processes in R and use the results to check analytic answers and estimate hard quantities.

units.title: Probability theory
topics: Sample spaces, events, set operations; axioms of probability
Counting: permutations, combinations, multinomials; birthday problem and hash collisions
Conditional probability, multiplication rule, law of total probability
Bayes' theorem: medical tests, spam filters, malaria rapid tests with false positives
Independence and conditional independence; reliability of series and parallel systems

units.title: Random variables
topics: Discrete random variables, probability mass functions, cumulative distribution functions
Continuous random variables, probability density functions; the CDF as the bridge
Expectation, variance, standard deviation; linearity of expectation
Functions of random variables; expectation of a function
Indicator variables and counting with expectation (expected number of collisions, fixed points)

units.title: Special distributions
topics: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, negative binomial, hypergeometric
Poisson distribution and the Poisson process: arrivals at a bank, packets at a router
Uniform, exponential (memorylessness) and gamma distributions
Normal distribution: standardisation, tables, the 68-95-99.7 rule; normal approximation to binomial
Choosing a distribution for a real situation; fitting and checking in R

units.title: Moments and moment generating functions
topics: Moments about the origin and about the mean; skewness and kurtosis
Moment generating functions: definition, computing moments, uniqueness
MGFs of the standard distributions; sums of independent random variables
Characteristic functions and probability generating functions in brief

units.title: Joint probability distributions
topics: Joint, marginal and conditional distributions for discrete and continuous pairs
Independence of random variables; covariance and correlation
Conditional expectation and the law of iterated expectation
Sums of random variables, convolution; distribution of the maximum and minimum
Bivariate normal distribution; transformations of two variables

units.title: Special probability theorems
topics: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities; Chernoff bounds for randomised algorithms
Weak and strong laws of large numbers
Central limit theorem: statement, intuition and simulation
Applications: Monte Carlo estimation, error in polling, load on a server

units.title: Statistics: estimation and testing
topics: Descriptive statistics, histograms, boxplots, sample mean and variance
Point estimation: method of moments, maximum likelihood; bias and consistency
Confidence intervals for means and proportions; t-distribution
Hypothesis testing: null and alternative, p-values, type I and II errors, z and t tests, chi-square tests
Simple linear regression and correlation; A/B testing a web page

units.title: Computer simulation in R
topics: Pseudo-random numbers; sample, runif, rnorm, rbinom and friends; setting seeds
Simulating games, queues and random walks; estimating probabilities and expectations
Inverse transform and rejection sampling to generate any distribution
Bootstrap confidence intervals; visualising sampling distributions
Project: simulate a mobile-money transaction system or a classroom's exam scores and compare with theory

schedule.title: Probability foundations and counting
schedule.exercise: Solve eight counting problems by hand, including the birthday problem for a class of 40, and check each against a simulation.

tasks.title: List the sample space for two dice, compute the probabilities of five events by counting, and confirm them with a simulation of 10000 rolls
Compute the probability of a hash collision among n random 16-bit values for several n and compare with the birthday approximation
Apply the law of total probability to a three-supplier quality problem and check the answer with a Monte Carlo run of 100000 items

schedule.title: Bayes and independence
schedule.exercise: Explain in plain words why a positive result on an accurate test can still mean a low chance of disease, using a numeric example.

tasks.title: Compute the probability of malaria given a positive rapid test for a given prevalence, sensitivity and specificity, and tabulate the four outcomes
Train a spam filter on word counts with Bayes' theorem and test it on ten messages, reporting its false positive and false negative counts
Compare the reliability of series, parallel and mixed designs for a mobile-money server, and find the cheapest design that meets 99.9 percent availability

schedule.title: Random variables and expectation
schedule.exercise: Derive the mean and variance of a fair die and of the sum of two dice, then verify with a simulation.

tasks.title: Tabulate the pmf and CDF of the number of heads in four tosses, plot both, and compute the mean
Define a density on an interval, check that it integrates to one, compute probabilities from its CDF, and plot the density and the CDF together
Use linearity of expectation to find the mean of a sum of dependent variables, then check it with a simulation of 100000 trials

schedule.title: Functions of random variables and indicators
schedule.exercise: Use indicator variables to find the expected number of fixed points of a random permutation of n items, and show the answer does not depend on n.

tasks.title: Find the expectation of a squared die roll and of twice a die roll plus one, then compare them with simulated averages
Compute the expected number of collisions when hashing 100 keys into 365 slots with indicator variables and verify it by simulation
Derive the distribution of Y equal to X squared for a continuous X, plot it, and check it against a histogram of simulated values

schedule.title: Standard discrete and continuous distributions
schedule.exercise: Choose the right distribution for six real situations, such as customers arriving at a bank or defective items in a batch, and justify each.

tasks.title: Compute binomial probabilities for a batch of 20 items with a 5 percent defect rate and plot the pmf with its mean and spread
Model arrivals at a bank as a Poisson process, compute the chance of more than ten arrivals in an hour, and compare with simulated counts
Show the memoryless property of the exponential distribution by simulation and explain why a gamma distribution models waiting for the third event

schedule.title: The normal distribution and fitting
schedule.exercise: Standardise three values by hand, find probabilities from a table, and then check each with software.

tasks.title: Standardise exam scores with a given mean and spread and find the share of students above 70 using the normal curve
Approximate a binomial with a normal curve with continuity correction for several sample sizes and report the error of each approximation
Fit exponential, gamma and normal models to a data set of service times in R, compare them with a Q-Q plot, and choose the best model

schedule.title: Moments and generating functions
schedule.exercise: Show how to get the mean and variance from the moment generating function of a Poisson variable by differentiating.

tasks.title: Compute the first four moments, skewness and kurtosis of a small data set and say what each tells you about its shape
Derive the moment generating function of a binomial variable and use it to recover the mean and variance
Use MGFs to prove that the sum of independent Poisson variables is Poisson and confirm it by simulating 100000 sums

schedule.title: Joint distributions and conditioning
schedule.exercise: Compute the marginals, the covariance and the conditional expectation of a given joint pmf on a three-by-three grid by hand.

tasks.title: Build a joint probability table for two discrete variables and compute its marginal and conditional distributions
Compute covariance and correlation for a joint distribution, and give an example where the variables are uncorrelated but dependent
Verify the law of iterated expectation by computing the conditional expectation exactly and by simulation for a two-stage random process

schedule.title: Sums, extremes and the bivariate normal
schedule.exercise: Derive the distribution of the maximum of n independent uniform variables and explain what happens as n grows.

tasks.title: Compute the distribution of the sum of two dice by convolution and plot it against a simulation
Find the distribution of the minimum of the waiting times of three servers, each exponential, and test it with a simulation
Simulate bivariate normal data with a chosen correlation, plot the contours, and compare the conditional means with the theoretical regression line

schedule.title: Limit theorems
schedule.exercise: Prove the Chebyshev inequality in a few lines and use it to bound the chance a sample mean is far from the true mean.

tasks.title: Plot the running average of 5000 coin tosses for several runs and observe the law of large numbers in action
Simulate the sampling distribution of the mean for uniform, exponential and skewed data at several sample sizes, and show the normal shape emerging
Estimate the margin of error of a poll of 1000 voters by theory and simulation, and find the sample size needed for a margin of 2 percent

schedule.title: Descriptive statistics and estimation
schedule.exercise: Compute a mean, median and standard deviation by hand for a small sample, then explain which summary you would report for skewed income data.

tasks.title: Draw a histogram and boxplot of 100 exam scores, compute the five-number summary and flag any outliers
Find the maximum likelihood estimate of the rate of an exponential distribution from data, and compare it with the method of moments
Compute 95 percent confidence intervals for a mean from 1000 simulated samples and check how often the true value is covered

schedule.title: Hypothesis testing and regression
schedule.exercise: Write a short report of an A/B test of two web page designs, giving the hypothesis, the test, the p-value and an honest conclusion.

tasks.title: Carry out a one-sample t test on 25 delivery times against a target, and state the hypotheses, the p-value and the conclusion
Fit a simple linear regression of exam score on study hours, report the slope, the correlation and a confidence interval, and plot the residuals
Run a chi-square test of independence on a table of survey data, compute the expected counts, and estimate the test's power by simulation

schedule.title: Simulation and the project
schedule.exercise: Project report: compare simulated results from your model with the theoretical values and explain every gap greater than the expected random error.

tasks.title: Generate 10000 uniform and normal random numbers with a fixed seed, show that the same seed repeats the run, and plot their histograms
Generate exponential samples by the inverse transform method and a triangular sample by rejection sampling, and compare each with its true density
Simulate a mobile-money transaction system with random arrivals and failures, and compare queue length and waiting time with the theoretical queue model
